# NOTES: TWO BOOKS

## BOOK 1 of 2: THE WORLD MASTERS (George Griffith, 1903)

**Prologue (Strassburg, night):** Dr Emil Fargeau (~60, Alsatian, ex-Prof. Physical Science, Strassburg Univ.) pacing attic lab over Fisher's Gate by River Ill. Round machine ~3 ft, glass cover, 4 glass supports, silk wires to batteries. Steel plate 4in sq, 1in thick, under ring of needles. Cuckoo clock. He strikes plate with wooden mallet; it shatters. Vows to break Germany ("Blood and Iron"). Claims "Soul of the World"/living principle of matter; wants France (his "mother") mistress of world; Adelaide and son Victor to rule France with Prince de Condé on throne. Money: ten 20-mark gold pieces, ~25 marks more. Sold farms; mortgaged to Jew money-lender Reuss Weinthal (Judenstrasse, Strassburg), draft with a month to run; he altered figures. Plans Paris "to-morrow."

**Ch I (27 Jan, Kaiser's birthday, German Embassy, Nevski Prospekt, Petersburg):**
- Prince Louis Xavier de Condé, Duc de Montpensier (~50), Bourbon features, voluntary exile, hates French Republic; wears Order of St Vladimir, Golden Fleece.
- Adelaide de Condé, Marquise de Montpensier (<21), "Marie Antoinette" look.
- Capt. Victor Fargeau (~28), Uhlan, military attaché German Embassy Petersburg, dark blue eyes; Adelaide and he share a long clasp.
- French Ambassador absent (sent regrets; Sophie says he met Count Lansdorf and "Little Father").
- Count Leo Valdemar, Chief of Third Section, Ministry of Interior; big, bearded. Daughter Countess Sophie Valdemar (19): fair, golden-bronze hair, pansy-blue eyes, sensuous full lips; "most skilful diplomatic detective in Europe"; hates Adelaide.
- Victor, called away by lacquey; later in winter garden tells Adelaide "he has succeeded," "goes to Paris to-morrow." Sophie overhears fragments, schemes.

**Ch II:**
- Paris, French Minister of War. Fargeau's pleas; Minister refuses without proof, sneers "Pfennige," offers 50-franc note. Fargeau: "Through you France has refused it... On your heads be it."
- Before leaving Strassburg he destroyed essential parts of accumulator. Hotel nearly broke (~100 francs).
- Letters: to Victor (German Embassy, Petersburg); to Reuss Weinthal (Strassburg); undated/unsigned one with specs in air-tight tin case.
- Tin strapped to small of back. Second-class ticket Nord Station to Southampton via le Havre. Midnight mid-Channel: "Tant pis pour toi"; jumps overboard into screws. Body and tin lashed together float away.

**Ch III (May, Channel, steam yacht *Nadine*):**
- Owner Ernest Shafto Hardress, Viscount Branston (eldest son of Earl of Orrel); guest Frank Lamson (M.A. Cambridge, D.Sc. London, 32, gold medal). Lamson spots body; Hardress stops yacht; body sewn in canvas by Mr Jackson's crew; tin box found tied to body.
- Lady Olive (Hardress's sister, ~25, dark Irish eyes). Miss Chrysie Vandel (daughter of Clifford K. Vandel, President, American Electrical Storage Trust, Buffalo NY; golden hair, deep blue eyes; large mouth). Kipling "Seven Seas" spat; "Kipling's good, but breakfast's better."
- Lamson to open box alone.

**Ch IV:** Lamson reads manuscript, locks door, temptation: "Master of the world." Keeps papers in hip-pocket. Asks Hardress "How would you like to be master of the world?" Describes "electrolising" the *Nadine* (boilers, hull shatter). Hardress: "Great Caesar's ghost!"; will join with Vandel; Morgan Steel Trust mention. Lamson: needs ~$1–2 million; "could be everything a mortal ought not to be."

**Ch V (Orrel Court, South Downs, Hampshire; ~fortnight later):**
- Harry Shafto Hardress, 8th Earl of Orrel (~50+), dead American wife's millions.
- Clifford K. Vandel ("Lightning King"), commands US electricity/wireless (Etherography) from Buffalo/NY; old Southern aristocrat sympathies, contempt for democracy; uncle of late Lady Orrel.
- Dinner talk: climate control for Britain; Lamson's scruple ("too splendid for human responsibility"); Chrysie's "Beaconsfield" jab; men talk business; Vandel's nightly vow "Masters of the world."

**Ch VI:**
- Vandel = president/financial manager of "International Magnetic Control Syndicate."
- Lamson studies US electrical machinery.
- Hardress obtains lease of Boothia Felix (Boothia Land, magnetic pole) from Canada: £1000/yr for 10 yrs; cover = observatory for Northern Lights, wireless.
- Buffalo: Hardress proposes to Chrysie on Empire State Express. Her answer: "not going to say 'Yes' right away"; wants love; he kisses hand ("syllabus," "option on territory," "reserve"). Vandel consents ("I'd sooner she chose you").
- Prince and Adelaide to Petersburg night mail.

**Ch VII (Elsenau, Hôtel Wilhelmshof, Thuringian/Hartz area; mineral spring for gout):**
- Lord Orrel and Lady Olive on verandah; prince and Adelaide arrive. Olive and Adelaide become "new friends."
- Orrel–prince friendship from Aix-les-Bains six years earlier; Orrel's younger brother served French army in 1870, killed by communards.
- Democracy-degeneration talk. Prince reveals "Alsatian scientist" who had "soul of the earth," which Orrel recognizes.

**Ch VIII:**
- Orrel tells whole story (Channel body, tin box). Prince cries "Mon Dieu... It is the same!" ; collapses in grief/rage. Says Fargeau was his son's father-in-law-to-be pact (daughter for son).
- Prince sleeps, then madness (family curse) in night; rings for valet Felix; sends for Adelaide; she sees delirium, learns story; opiate.
- Dies at sunrise; broken blood vessel. Last words: "France! O ma belle France, maitresse du monde--et moi ton roi." Resident physician certifies.
- Hardress arrives that evening.

**Ch IX:**
- Funeral; prince buried in brick grave under Elsenau pines (Republic bars return to France).
- Hardress fetches Madame de Condé (Princess of Bourbon) from Vienna.
- Adelaide's padded Russia-leather diary (silver key, shorthand). Entry: sold herself to Victor; Hardress "master of the world," admired; ends "I wonder if there is another woman?"

**Ch X:**
- Lord Orrel/Hardress talk: Hardress loves Chrysie, not Adelaide.
- Vienna: Adelaide tells Victor their discovery is in Englishmen's hands; plan to go to Paris. Victor resigns German commission, plans to offer France his duplicate papers; "Henceforth I am a Frenchman." Adelaide now resents him; kiss "must be the last."

**Ch XI:** Victor in Paris (Avenue de l'Opéra), contacts secretary Gaston Leraulx (Ministry of War). Meets Adelaide (Avenue Neuilly); plans interview with General Ducros. Valdemars' condolence visit; Sophie spies on Victor; mentions Boothia Land lease.

**Ch XII:**
- Russian trapper's telegram from Montreal (re Hardress deal) reaches Sophie/Count; Ducros also gets voyageur's telegram. Ducros regrets rejecting Fargeau.
- Ducros dinner with Valdemars; Sophie demands use of private room adjoining Ducros's bureau for the interview.
- Next day interview: Victor, Adelaide present (Sophie listening). Victor's plan: Arctic expedition of old warships (like *Alert*, *Discovery*) with guns, to seize works in ~a year. Ducros agrees; Russia must be ally.

**Ch XIII (Cowes week, ~1 year later, Orrel Court):**
- Chrysie tells father Clifford Vandel of Adelaide's rivalry; father notes French/Russian expeditions; cable to Lamson.
- Sophie/Adelaide suspected of spying.

**Ch XIV:**
- Sophie and Count at Orrel Court: Count's spies; Sophie's plan to seize *Nadine* (Lord Orrel, Hardress, Vandel, Lamson's? wife Lady Olive, Chrysie, Adelaide) mid-Atlantic with yacht *Vlodoya*.
- Seduced second engineer Edward Williams (embittered inventor; Hardress rejected submarine plan); promised £5,000 gold + Russian dockyard post.
- Vandel cables Lamson: French/Russian expeditions "for capture or destruction of Storage Works."

**Ch XV (Boothia Land, "Port Adelaide" works):**
- Works: 400 ft square; central 40-ft tower with absorber (reproduction of Fargeau's apparatus); four 2000-hp engines; Austin Vandel (nephew, GM, telegraph); Lamson's disintegrator; telegraph via Winnipeg; steel masts 300 ft at 200-mile intervals across Canada/Greenland/Iceland/Britain.
- Lamson: decides to bring party to works; will not start engines (would cut US communications).
- Chrysie-Vandel: Sophie's maid's brother Jules (spy-servant).

**Ch XVI:**
- Adelaide gets Victor's letter: expeditions ready; Russian ice-breaker *Ivan the Terrible*.
- Lawn talk: Chrysie vs Sophie; Hardress tells news of German officer/extradition.
- Sophie plans to make Adelaide ally; Count's cable: war imminent.

**Ch XVII:** Sophie persuades Adelaide (who loves Hardress) to join, offers Bourbon restoration promise. Adelaide demands oath: no harm to Hardress, father, sister; Chrysie watches them.

**Ch XVIII:**
- Count and Sophie sail on *Vlodoya* to Cherbourg; Felice (Adelaide's maid) telegram to Count: "Nadine starts this evening... Dépêchez."
- Williams paid; Hardress orders coal, full speed; Vandel's council. Telegram duplicate taken by Chrysie.

**Ch XIX:**
- *Nadine* leaves Southampton (4pm), full speed 20 knots. Captain Burgess; M'Niven (chief engineer); Williams nervous; Hardress suspects him.
- Adelaide and Williams glance at deck.

**Ch XX:**
- Vandelite gun (Vandel's invention, 12-pound liquid-gas gun) mounted; Maxims on bridge.
- Chrysie confronts Adelaide, shows revolver; Adelaide in fear.
- Williams caught sanding driving rod, grits port shaft; port engine failed; speed down to ~8 knots. Williams under arrest.

**Ch XXI:**
- Adelaide's "punch à la Grand Monarque" served; Chrysie and Vandel avoid it; Captain Burgess, M'Niven abstain. Drug knocks out ship's company incl. Lord Orrel, Hardress, Lady Olive, Madame de Bourbon, Adelaide. Vandel and Chrysie awake; Vernon (chief officer) abstains; hose-down revives crew.
- *Vlodoya* overtakes ~daybreak.

**Ch XXII (naval duel):**
- Vlodoya shells; Chrysie at Maxim; Vandel's gun hits Vlodoya's stern; second shot kills Maxim forecastle; Vlodoya stops.
- Count and Sophie on bridge; "Hands up, please."

**Ch XXIII:**
- Vlodoya's captain killed by Chrysie; Count and Sophie taken on board; Count "Mr Vandel... fortune of war."
- Vlodoya's crew set adrift; Vlodoya's coal transferred; sunk by Vandelite gun. Dinner; Adelaide's "punch" accused; Nadine heads to Boothia Land.

**Ch XXIV:**
- Press frenzy; *Globe* leader; Germany demands Victor's extradition; France refuses; Russia's note; both expeditions sail. Trust circular (Buffalo, NY; London office 56b Old Broad St): capitation fee $1/man/week; one week to settle; threat to cut electricity; new disease.
- Governments scoff; Paris understands.

**Ch XXV:**
- Works run for 6 days. Engines started at six p.m./a.m. by Chrysie's lever (Hardress: "save life"; Adelaide's "magic"); Lady Olive presses button.
- French squadron off Elbe/Kiel: compasses wander, shafts break, guns burst; *Charles Martel* drifts to Elbe mud; Brunsbüttel fort gun bursts; locomotives fail.

**Ch XXVI:**
- Europe paralysed; soldiers starving. Kaiser and President Loubet cross to England. Meet at Claridge's; go to Marlborough House with King Edward. Agree to arbitration. Count Russian minister "must wire St Petersburg."
- Russian ice-breaker + 3 ships reach Adelaide Bay; French squadron follows.

**Ch XXVII:**
- Ships anchor ~4 miles from works; frank hostility visible (Russian ice-breaker 6-in guns; French 100-lb shells).
- Adelaide and Sophie plan murder; Adelaide wants Chrysie and Hardress dead. Sophie gives Adelaide Chrysie's stolen revolver (Sophie's pickpocketing).
- Count says Orrel invited the admirals to dinner (incl. Victor).

**Ch XXVIII:**
- Tea on wall: Chrysie wears seven-shooter. Lamson's telegram from King Edward ("Edward R.I."): Powers agree arbitration if engines stop. Hardress agrees to switch off.
- Dinner in board-room, 8 p.m.: Vice-Adm. Alexis Nazanoff (Russian); Prof. Josef Karnina; Vice-Adm. Dumont (French); Victor Fargeau. Lord Orrel's welcome; Nazanoff refuses surrender; Hardress: "annihilated."

**Ch XXIX:**
- Victor's claim; Dumont gives until 6 a.m.; Lord Orrel refuses. Lamson's defences: searchlights, copper tubes, disintegrator rays from 4 towers, 8 gun platforms.
- Sophie sings Russian hymn; Lady Olive sings "God Save the King"; refuses to shake hands.
- At gate: Adelaide shoots Hardress (broken thigh), Chrysie (arm), Sophie fires; Adelaide, Sophie and Victor are struck by disintegrator ray, reduced to bones.

**Ch XXX:** Hardress and Chrysie carried in. Orrel tells Madame de Bourbon; she goes to *Corneille*. Williams handed over. Count begs Nazanoff for revenge.

**Ch XXXI:**
- 6 a.m.: searchlights blaze; Count fires first shot on *Ivan*; dies to disintegrator ray from lighthouse on north point. Admiral Dumont killed on *Caiman*.
- Works' guns (6 hundred-lb Vandelite shells) destroy French and Russian ships; survivors on *Ivan* and *Caiman* (only *Ivan* survives).
- *Corneille* takes Madame de Bourbon and bone casket of Adelaide to France; Sophie and Count's bones to Petersburg (brother's house near German Embassy).

**Epilogue:** Hardress and Chrysie recover; Lamson announces Powers "surrendered"; arbitration by Pope/Archbishop of Canterbury/Archimandrite; Chrysie: "We four... run the world." Hardress/Chrysie kiss; "contract... sign, seal, and deliver." THE END.

## BOOK 2 of 2: THE LADY OF THE FOREST (L. T. Meade, A Story for Girls)

**Ch I (Avonsyde, New Forest):**
- Rachel (12, dark, gypsy-faced, storyteller) and Kitty (9, fair, blue eyes) with Aunt Griselda ("Aunt Grizel," Miss Griselda Lovel, stern) and Aunt Katharine ("Kitty," soft). Philip Lovel expected next day.
- History: Rupert Lovel disinherited (left 20 Aug 1684); younger son Valentine got Avonsyde. Rhyme: "Tyde what may betyde, / Lovel shall dwell at Avonsyde."
- Dying squire (their father): orders search for Rupert's descendant, a strong, manly boy, to be heir. Valentine's children appear in bedroom: Rachel ("Rachel Valentine Lovel") and Kitty. Squire: Rachel resembles Rupert; Kitty weak like Valentine. Squire: "Rupert's child."

**Ch II:** Mother (Rachel Lovel, née Cunningdale; in London lodgings) makes terms with sisters: children kept at Avonsyde; she may reclaim them on Rachel's 13th birthday (5 May). Mother leaves without kissing them. Squire dies blessing grandchildren.

**Ch III:** Five years pass. Phil and his mother (Bella Lovel) expected; Aunt Griselda hopes boy is heir. Rachel plans to go round world for mother at 15. Rachel secretly visits forest lady (in green/gray) at cottage via Nancy White.

**Ch IV:** Phil (8, pale, brown eyes, Spartan, secret side-pain) and Bella arrive by train; Bella coached Phil to lie (Melbourne claims, "Mexico" birth). Phil: "Is it antediluvian?" Griselda, Katharine greet; Newbolt maid. Griselda demands pedigree.

**Ch V:** Phil and Kitty in forest. Rachel rides Surefoot with groom Robert into forest; meets Nancy White outside lady's cottage; Rachel promises secrecy (no telling Kitty or aunts). Nancy: lady is "lonely," must hide.

**Ch VI:** Tower bedroom (7 centuries old; heir sleeps there, ladies above). Bella dislikes room. Phil speaks of Rupert; Bella fears exposure; plans to leave.

**Ch VII (Belmont, near Melbourne):** Rupert Lovel (15, strong), Gabrielle (13, housekeeper), Peggy (small, flaxen, ravens Elijah and James Grasper). Phil's letter (misspelled, begs them to write to "Master Phil Lovel, Post-office, To be called for," Southampton). Aunt Bella's mysterious departure (sold house, took £200). Betty O'Flanigan (old Irish servant). Father Rupert Lovel senior: advertisement in *Melbourne Times* (Messrs. Baring & Baring, 128 Chancery Lane) for heirs of Rupert Lovel; Griselda/Katharine's own advert. Tankard (silver, "Betyde what may," family crest) and letters said missing; a cheap false tankard found in cupboard.

**Ch VIII:** Gabrielle searches "sacred cupboard" in dead mother's room; Rupert prays at her sofa. Cupboard relics; tankard gone.

**Ch IX:** Rachel's trysting place (oak tree in glade); Nancy: "lady" will see Rachel on 13th birthday. Rachel gives Nancy her gold ring with pearl for the lady. Nancy asks Rachel to bring Phil secretly.

**Ch X:** Griselda's "proofs" conditions; Bella asks what if no heir; Griselda offers £500/yr for Bella if heir found. Bella: "Am I not to live at Avonsyde always?"

**Ch XI:** Kitty/Rachel/Phil secret talk about lady of forest (green, gift of beauty). Phil (wants bag of gold). Phil finds silver tankard in old trunk in tower; takes it.

**Ch XII:** Phil lost in New Forest at dawn; in bog; robins lead lady to him. He faints; she rescues him.

**Ch XIII:** Phil in lady's cottage; lady asks secrecy; Phil's "Rachel looks like her." Lady: "I am no supernatural lady." Nancy finds tankard (Phil's) on floor; keeps it. Bella (mother) overhears.

**Ch XIV:** Baring's office: Bella (Rachel Cunningdale's version) interviewed. Australian Rupert Lovel senior & son Rupert arrive; Mrs Lovel = Rachel Cunningdale, Rupert senior's late wife's friend. Her full story: husband Valentine's death (consumption); her poverty; Kitty fainted from hunger; she sold ring, dressed girls, brought them to Avonsyde; terms with sisters; forest cottage lent by friends.

**Ch XV:** Phil's secret attack in armory; Kitty runs for Bella; Bella says "acting." Phil tells Rachel of cottage; Rachel says she knows.

**Ch XVI:** Bella's background; Phil writes to Rupert; Bella travels to Southampton, gets Rupert's letter from post office; discovers tankard missing; "Then we are lost."

**Ch XVII:** Phil's regret; plans to find tankard in forest; Marmadukes announced (Clementina, Dick, Will, Abby; parrot, pug).

**Ch XVIII:** Marmaduke picnic at Rufus' Stone; Clementina rides Ruby (Rachel's red-coated colt; Robert warns). Phil visits cottage; Nancy says she has not seen tankard.

**Ch XIX:** Phil meets lady; she walks with him; Rachel sees her from oak tree; lady kisses hand toward Rachel. Phil: "Rachel's heart is hungrier."

**Ch XX:** Ruby bolts; Clementina thrown into bog; Phil and Robert rescue her; Phil's lecture; Phil rests in "nest." Bella confronted by Clementina.

**Ch XXI:** Griselda fond of Phil; "the heir ought to be" talk (wants Rupert's likeness). Rhyme "Come what may come, tyde what may tyde..."; Griselda plans Eton prep school.

**Ch XXII:** Rupert senior tells Baring they won't claim until tankard and letters found; refuses to take property; Nancy hides tankard, keeps it.

**Ch XXIII:** Spring in forest; Phil's nature finds; Nancy with tankard in cupboard.

**Ch XXIV:** Griselda invites Rachel's mother (Mrs Valentine Lovel, 10 Abbey Street, Marshall Road, SW London) for 5 May. Bella produces no tankard; Nancy's rhyme note "Tankards to the right are given." Bella faints/sleeps in forest; Nancy finds her.

**Ch XXV:** Phil's dream: lady says "Look for him on the 5th of May... Farewell." Bella resolves to give up Avonsyde.

**Ch XXVI:** Bella's letter to Griselda: going to London to see Baring. Telegrams from Baring; he goes to forest cottage with Bella and Rupert senior and junior. Bella confesses theft to Baring; tankard/letters evidence.

**Ch XXVII:** Lady of forest's letter (invitation 5 May). Baring & Australians at cottage. Bella's confession; "Two mothers." Phil's evening with Griselda and Katharine; organ; Phil asks Griselda about the lady.

**Ch XXVIII (5 May):** Party at Avonsyde; Bella (in black velvet, crimson rose) confesses publicly; Rupert (true heir) arrives with Phil. Rachel and Kitty reunited with their mother (lady of forest). Phil and Rupert walk to forest; Phil sees "the lady," then dies in Rupert's arms. Last line: "That is the story. Sad? Perhaps so--not sad for Phil." THE END.
